'''''Illecebrum''''' is a [[monotypic taxon|monotypic]] genus in the family [[Caryophyllaceae]]. It contains the single species '''''Illecebrum verticillatum''''', which is a trailing [[annual plant]] native to Europe, with whorls of small white flowers borne in the axils of the paired leaves.

==Distribution==
''Illecebrum verticillatum'' is native to much of [[Europe]], from the western [[Iberian Peninsula]] to [[Poland]];<ref name="FAE"/> it is rare in [[Great Britain]],<ref name="Stace"/> and its northernmost station is in [[Denmark]].<ref name="FAE">{{cite book |editor=Jaakko Jalas & Juha Suominen |year=1998 |series=Atlas Florae Europaeae: Distribution of Vascular Plants in Europe |volume=6 |title=Caryophyllaceae (Alsinoideae and Paronychioideae) |publisher=[[Cambridge University Press]] |isbn=978-0-521-34272-8 |page=154 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=8XIJ1rWpwcMC&pg=PA154}}</ref> It has also been [[introduced species]] to at least one site in [[New Zealand]] and one site in [[Western Australia]].<ref name="Wilson"/>

==Description==
''Illecebrum verticillatum'' produces procumbent or decumbent (trailing) [[plant stem|stems]] that may be up to {{convert|20|cm|abbr=on}} high. It has ovate leaves arranged in opposite pairs along the stem. The small [[flower]]s are clustered in the [[leaf axil|axils of the leaves]]; their [[petal]]s are much smaller than the white [[sepal]]s.<ref name="Stace">{{cite book |author=Clive A. Stace |author-link=Clive A. Stace |year=2010 |title=New Flora of the British Isles |edition=3rd |publisher=[[Cambridge University Press]] |isbn=978-0-521-70772-5 |pages=466–467 |chapter=''Illecebrum'' L. – coral-necklace}}</ref>

==Taxonomy==
''Illecebrum verticillatum'' was [[species description|first described]] by [[Carl Linnaeus]] in his 1753 ''[[Species Plantarum]]''. It has sometimes been placed in a family of its own, Illecebraceae, but is usually placed in the family [[Caryophyllaceae]].<ref name="Wilson"/> The genus name ''Illecebrum'' derives from the [[Latin]] word ''{{lang|la|[[:wikt:illecebra|illecebra]]}}'', meaning "enticement", although it is unclear how the name came to be applied to a plant such as ''I. verticillatum''.<ref name="Wilson"/> The [[specific name (botany)|specific epithet]] ''{{lang|la|[[:wikt:verticillatus|verticillatum]]}}'' means "whorled",<ref>{{cite book |author=David Gledhill |year=2002 |title=The Names of Plants |url=https://archive.org/details/namesofplants0000gled |url-access=registration |edition=3rd |publisher=[[Cambridge University Press]] |isbn=0-521-52340-0}}</ref> in reference to the arrangement of the flowers. The plant is sometimes referred to in published works as ''whorled knotweed'' or ''coral necklace'', although it is unclear if these purported [[common name]]s are actually used in practice.<ref name="Wilson">{{cite journal |author=Paul G. Wilson |year=1998 |title=''Illecebrum verticillatum'' (Caryophyllaceae), a new record for Australia |journal=[[Nuytsia (journal)|Nuytsia]] |volume=12 |issue=1 |pages=155–156 |doi=10.58828/nuy00289 |url=http://florabase.dpaw.wa.gov.au/science/nuytsia/289.pdf |access-date=2013-10-10 |archive-date=2018-04-11 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180411092905/https://florabase.dpaw.wa.gov.au/science/nuytsia/289.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref>
